source.snippet: I have a website that used to be hosted on Squarespace and is now a vanilla HTML/CSS site hosted on Netlify. When I inspect my site on Google Search Console, there are about fifteen thousand URLs that I don't recognize (I should only have 89 according to my sitemap which looks correct). When I go to these URLs in my browser, I get a 404. The unknown URLs aren't being indexed. I don't recognize the referring URL, which also 404s.

problem_statement: Website owners who migrate platforms (e.g., Squarespace to Netlify/static hosting) find thousands of phantom or legacy URLs polluting their Google Search Console coverage report, with no automated tool to diagnose the source, bulk-disavow crawl spam, or reconcile GSC data against their actual sitemap.
target_segment: Small business owners and indie web developers who self-manage SEO after a site migration
notes: Buyer signal: business website owner context; SEO tools are a well-established paid category (Ahrefs, Semrush, Screaming Frog all charge). Post-migration GSC cleanup is a recurring pain. The specific gap is automated reconciliation between GSC reported URLs and current sitemap + identification of spam referrers. Moderate buyer intent — these owners typically pay for SEO tools or hire agencies. Single signal but a common post-migration scenario.
